content.title: Invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS
content.summary: Guidance on timing and indications for invasive coronary strategy in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes (NSTE-ACS).

recommendations.indication: NSTE-ACS patients with high-risk criteria or a high index of suspicion for unstable angina
recommendations.notes: Recommend invasive strategy during hospital admission for high-risk or high suspicion patients.

recommendations.indication: Patients without very high- or high-risk NSTE-ACS criteria and with a low index of suspicion for NSTE-ACS
recommendations.notes: Selective invasive strategy recommended for lower-risk patients.

recommendations.indication: Patients with a working diagnosis of NSTE-ACS and at least one very high-risk criterion
very_high_risk_criteria: Recurrent or refractory chest pain despite medical treatment
Acute heart failure presumed secondary to ongoing myocardial ischaemia
Recurrent dynamic ST‑segment or T‑wave changes, particularly intermittent ST‑segment elevation
recommendations.notes: Immediate invasive strategy for any of listed very high-risk features.

recommendations.indication: Patients with at least one high-risk criterion
high_risk_criteria: Confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI based on current recommended ESC hs-cTn algorithms
Dynamic ST-segment or T wave changes
recommendations.notes: Consider early invasive approach within 24 hours when any high-risk criterion present.

abbreviations.GRACE: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
abbreviations.hs-cTn: high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (algorithm referenced, not a gene name)

content.references_note: References cited in the figure (numerical citations shown) and supplementary data referenced for ST-segment elevation equivalents.
